consumer_seed: The Connected Nations Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The report is a snapshot of UK mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of 30.5 million homes.
An additional 1.2 million homes gained access to full fibre in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up across residential and commercial premises reached 12.4 million, an increase of 1.8 million.
The 12.4 million full-fibre connections represented 47% of premises with access to full fibre.
Gigabit-capable broadband availability reached 89% of UK homes, or 27.1 million homes.
Gigabit-capable availability was 87%, or 26.4 million homes, in July 2025.
The report estimated 4,000 premises without access to affordable decent broadband.
The number unable to access decent broadband by fixed line or fixed wireless access fell to 39,000 from 44,000.
Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all mobile network operators reached 84% of UK landmass.
Predicted 4G geographic coverage from at least one mobile network operator remained at 96% of UK landmass.
Outdoor 5G standalone coverage ranged from 49% to 85% across the three operators that had deployed it.
Outdoor coverage from all operators for overall 5G increased from 47% to 64%.
The Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage checker page was published on 17 August 2022.
The coverage checker page was last updated on 25 June 2025.
The mobile and broadband checkers accept a postcode to show mobile coverage by provider or broadband-service availability.
The broadband checker presents standard, superfast and ultrafast service categories.
Checker results can also be viewed as interactive maps.
Fixed-broadband and mobile data are available to developers through Ofcom APIs.
The coverage checker does not show maintenance or reported network issues; users are directed to provider status information.
Ofcom uses Ordnance Survey data as the base property dataset for the broadband checker.
The base property data is updated in the checker twice a year.
The checker FAQ defines standard broadband as download speeds up to 30 Mbit/s.
The checker FAQ defines ultrafast broadband as download speeds above 300 Mbit/s.
Fixed Wireless Access may use a mobile or dedicated wireless network and its displayed coverage is based on predictive modelling.
A person unable to obtain 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload may request an upgraded connection subject to USO eligibility.
No displayed prediction for an address does not necessarily mean broadband is unavailable.
Received speed can differ from checker predictions because of in-building networks, simultaneous device use and line condition.
Ofcom published the emergency-calls compliance programme on 31 October 2025.
The emergency-calls compliance programme closed on 8 June 2026.
General Conditions require regulated providers to take all necessary measures for uninterrupted access to emergency organisations in voice services.
Providers must make accurate and reliable caller-location information available for 999 and 112 calls where technically feasible.
The programme identified General Conditions A3.2(b), A3.5 and A3.6 as relevant provisions.
Ofcom found no specific issues warranting further formal enforcement action when the programme closed.
Ofcom stated that it would continue monitoring compliance and could take enforcement action if serious concerns arise.
